# Win probability, expectancy and honest feedback

*Generated by `python3 tools/win_probability.py`.  The numbers below are
derived from the shipped configuration, the measured ATR of the symbols the
scanner picks, and 30 000-path Monte-Carlo runs on the exit distribution
described in `app/analytics/compound.py`.*

## 0. Headline

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| P(a single trade wins) | **~45-50%** -- a coin flip before fees |
| break-even win rate | **45.7%** (band: 44-52%) |
| P(account green after a week) | **45%** |
| P($20 -> $10,000 in 7 days), realistic exits | **< 0.01%** (0 of 30,000 simulated weeks) |
| P($20 -> $10,000 in 7 days), every winner books the +200% ROI TP | **< 0.01%** (0 of 30,000 simulated weeks) |

The +200% ROI take-profit is the only reason the target arithmetic works at
all, and it needs a **+20% price move** inside one trade. Treat the target as
a stress metric; treat the trailing ladder as the strategy.

## 1. What a trade actually is

* risk per trade: **8% of equity**, leverage **10x** -> notional = **80% of equity**
* stop: 3xATR, which for the picked symbols (5m ATR 0.65-1.65%, median 0.95%) is **-20% to -49% ROI**, i.e. **-1.6% to -4.0% of equity per loser**
* take profit: +200% ROI on margin = **+16.0% of equity**, but it requires a
  **+20.0% price move** (200% / 10x) -- that is **21x ATR** on a 5m chart for the median
  symbol. It is a tail event, not a plan.
* trailing: activates at +30% ROI (a +3.0% price move) and locks
  +20% ROI (+1.6% of equity) -- so the *typical winner is small* while the
  stop is wide. That inversion is the single most important finding here.

## 2. Break-even win rate

**as designed (every winner books +200% ROI)** -- upper bound

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| win rate in the sample | 45.0% |
| mean winner | +200.0% ROI |
| mean loser | -32.1% ROI |
| mean ROI per trade | +72.34% |
| **break-even win rate** | **13.8%** |

**realistic (2% of trades reach +200% ROI)** -- plan with this

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| win rate in the sample | 46.0% |
| mean winner | +38.3% ROI |
| mean loser | -32.2% ROI |
| mean ROI per trade | +0.22% |
| **break-even win rate** | **45.7%** |


Sensitivity (break-even win rate = mean loser / (mean loser + mean winner)):

| mean winner -> | +25% | +30% | +35% | +40% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean loser -25% | 50.0% | 45.5% | 41.7% | 38.5% |
| mean loser -30% | 54.5% | 50.0% | 46.2% | 42.9% |
| mean loser -35% | 58.3% | 53.8% | 50.0% | 46.7% |

So depending on the ATR regime and how much the trail gives back, break-even
sits in the **mid-40s to low-50s** -- exactly where a raw 5-minute divergence
signal sits before any real filter alpha.  Fees matter little by comparison:
a MEXC round trip is 0.4% of margin, Binance 1.0%, KuCoin 1.2%.

The important number is the **realistic break-even win rate: 45.7%** -- a raw 5-minute AO divergence has to
clear that bar *after* costs.  Independent AO backtests are not encouraging:
a long-only Bill-Williams AO study found the plain signal "far from tradable"
(average gain 0.57%) and only improved with a trend filter
(quantifiedstrategies.com/bill-williams-awesome-oscillator-strategy/); the
indicator "can give a lot of false signals during flat market"
(litefinance.org).  Vendor pages advertising 70-80% win rates for
oscillator-divergence scripts are selling the script, not the results.

*That is the honest answer to "what is the winning probability": roughly a
coin flip per trade, decided by whether the filter stack (trend alignment,
HTF EMA, volume, structure break, AO-delta vs ATR) actually adds edge.  The
paper-mode signal log is the experiment that answers it with your own data.*

## 3. Probability of being profitable

| horizon | trades | P(account above start) | median equity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 day | 8 | 44.4% | $19.73 |
| 1 week | 56 | 44.7% | $19.07 |
| 1 month | 240 | 42.0% | $16.40 |
| 1 year | 2920 | 25.4% | $3.97 |

Read that table honestly, because it hides the second trap: the **arithmetic**
mean ROI is +0.2%/trade while the **geometric** growth is slightly negative --
volatility drag.  A -32% ROI stop costs 2.56% of equity; the equally sized
winner only adds 3.04%, and the mix does not compound.  With 8% of equity at
10x per trade, a marginal edge is eaten by variance.  Smaller size per trade
(3-5%) fixes the drag far more reliably than a better entry signal does.

## 4. The target

* $20 -> $10,000 in 7 days is **500x**, i.e. **+143.0% per day, compounded**.
* with 8 trades/day that is **+11.74% of equity per trade**, every trade, for 56 trades.
* **designed**: P(reach $10,000 in 7 days) = **0.000%** (not observed in 30,000 simulated weeks (<0.003%)), P(ruin) = 0.0%, median $364.22
* **realistic**: P(reach $10,000 in 7 days) = **0.000%** (not observed in 30,000 simulated weeks (<0.003%)), P(ruin) = 0.0%, median $19.00
* required win rate for the target **with the +200% ROI TP filling**: 78.3% (break-even on that same model: 13.6%)

## 5. Feedback -- what to change to make it worth running

1. **Fix the risk/reward inversion.** The *typical* trail exit is +20-25% ROI
   while the 3xATR stop costs 25-35% ROI, so the median loser is ~1.4x the
   median winner -- you are risking more than the trade usually makes. Either
   widen the trail window (activate at +60% ROI, lock +30%) or take partial
   profit: close half at +50% ROI (about 1R) and let the rest run -- this is
   implemented as `takeprofit.partial_tp_enabled` (opt-in, off by default;
   see docs/RISK.md). Until the average winner clears the average loser, the
   required win rate stays above 46%.
2. **Treat the +200% ROI TP as a lottery ticket, not the exit.** Keep it on the
   exchange as a reduce-only order (it costs nothing and catches the tail), but
   plan expectancy off the trailing ladder.
3. **Cut concurrency.** 10 positions x 80% notional each = 8x equity of notional
   in assets that are 0.8-correlated. A single alt flush stops out the whole book
   at once: 10 losers = -22.8% of equity in one
   candle, which also trips the 25% daily-loss halt. 3-5 positions is the same
   edge with survivable tails.
4. **Prove the edge before risking money.** The dashboard's paper mode records
   every signal with its filter verdicts. Run it for a few days and look at
   accepted-vs-rejected outcomes -- if accepted signals do not beat rejected ones,
   the filters are decoration.
5. **Set an honest target.** $20 -> $25 in a week is a realistic goal;
   $20 -> $10,000 in a week requires +143%/day for 7 days and is not a plan,
   it is a lottery with a sub-1% jackpot.

---

*Reproduce: `python3 tools/win_probability.py --print` (add `--start/--target/--days` to re-run the growth ladder for another account size).*
